title: Insurance Defence Legal Assistant / Law Clerk
description:
About the Company

Forge Recruitment is proud to partner with a leading insurance defence litigation law firm in downtown Toronto. Known for their fast-paced, collaborative, and collegial environment, this firm is recognized for its deep expertise in tort and accident benefits (AB) work, as well as its commitment to professional growth, open communication, and flexible work arrangements.

About the Role

We are seeking a Legal Assistant / Law Clerk hybrid to support one of the firm's senior litigators, and occasional clerking support to other team members. This is an exciting opportunity to be part of a dynamic, fast-moving tort and AB litigation practice (approximately 60% tort / 40% AB).

The position offers a reduced billable target to reflect the dual nature of assistant and clerking responsibilities, and is ideal for someone who enjoys variety, wants to grow their skills, and thrives in a collaborative environment.

Assistant Responsibilities

  • Scheduling discoveries, mediations, defence medicals, and other key litigation events.

  • Calendar management and tracking deadlines.

  • Opening and closing files.

  • Coordinating accounts and billing.

  • Maintaining electronic and physical filing systems.

  • Providing day-to-day administrative support to the lead lawyer.

Law Clerk Responsibilities

  • Reviewing and summarizing files and briefs.

  • Drafting pleadings and affidavits (with senior support for more complex matters).

  • Supporting with trial preparation, including witness scheduling and trial binders.

  • Scheduling defence medicals and coordinating with experts.

  • Assisting with strategy execution and practice organization.

What You Bring

  • 3+ years' experience as a Legal Assistant and/or Law Clerk in insurance defence litigation (tort and/or AB experience preferred).

  • Strong organizational and calendar management skills.

  • Comfort working in a busy, fast-paced practice with multiple moving pieces.

  • A proactive, solution-oriented mindset — someone not afraid to speak up, offer suggestions, and contribute to making the practice more efficient.

  • Excellent communication skills and strong attention to detail.

  • Experience with MS Office and legal DMS systems.

  • Law Clerk experience is an asset but not mandatory — training will be provided for the right candidate who is eager to learn.

Work Environment & Culture

  • Supportive and approachable leadership style — no rigid hierarchy.

  • Encouragement to share ideas and perspectives to improve workflows.

  • Primarily remote practice. In-person attendance may be required for trials or occasional team events.

The Offer

  • Competitive, negotiable compensation package.

  • Full benefits package.

  • Permanent, full-time role with flexibility.

  • Exposure to high-level insurance defence work with leading litigators.

  • Ongoing training and development opportunities.


Next Steps

title: Wills and Estates Law Clerk
description:
About the Company
Our client, a full-service law firm in Central Ontario, is seeking an experienced Wills and Estates Law Clerk to join thir growing practice in Barrie, ON.

About the Role

You will join the Wills & Estates team as a key member supporting lawyers, paralegals, and clients. Your responsibilities will span file management, drafting and document preparation, client communication, and administrative support; ensuring the practice runs smoothly and clients receive high-quality service. This is a great opportunity for someone who is organized, detail-oriented, and enjoys working collaboratively in a dynamic legal environment.

  • Assist in the opening, maintenance and closing of wills and estates files; ensure accuracy of client data, conflict checks, billing setups, and file systems.

  • Draft and prepare legal documents under supervision, including wills, powers of attorney, trusts, letters of administration, estate reports, and court forms for estate administrators.

  • Manage document flow: assemble drafts, revisions, sign-offs, e-signatures, filings, and record-keeping in accordance with firm protocols and AODA standards.

  • Coordinate with clients, internal teams (lawyers, paralegals, administrative services) and external parties (trust companies, banks, government offices, executors) for meetings, instructions, document signing and closing matters.

  • Proofread correspondence and legal documents to ensure clarity, compliance, formatting consistency, and internal quality standards.

  • Maintain and track deadlines, key dates and action items (e.g., executors' filings, trust distributions, estate administration follow-up).

  • Support billing, time entry and disbursement functions in the practice group; assist lawyers in preparing client invoices and matter reports.

  • Participate in practice improvements: contribute ideas for process efficiencies, document templates, technology use and client service enhancements aligned with the firm's values of open communication and peace of mind.

  • Occasional coverage for other Wills & Estates team administrative tasks as needed, contributing to overall team flexibility and service excellence.


The Offer

  • Work with a respected, full-service regional law firm known for its strong community presence and team-oriented culture.

  • Join a practice group with a broad mandate: estate planning, trusts, administration and court-related applications - offering variety and growth potential.

  • Be part of a collaborative environment that values open communication, results-driven advice and client peace of mind.

  • Opportunity for professional development, exposure to senior counsel and diverse client matters.

  • Competitive compensation and benefits, in a supportive setting that values work/life balance.



What You Bring

  • Law clerk, paralegal or legal administrative experience, preferably 3-5 years (or more) in wills, estates or trust administration.

  • Experience preparing and working with wills, powers of attorney, trusts, estate administration and court applications is a strong asset.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to interact professionally with clients, executors, banks, trustees and colleagues.

  • High degree of organization and attention to detail: ability to manage multiple files, track deadlines and maintain documentation integrity.

  • Proficiency with legal practice software, document management systems, Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and willingness to adopt new tools.

  • Ability to work both independently and collaboratively; a positive, client-service oriented attitude aligned with the firm's values.

  • Strong sense of confidentiality, professionalism and ethics in handling sensitive estate and trust matters.

  • Post-secondary legal administrative or paralegal credential preferred; eligible or registered paralegal status is an asset.
